newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West electricity prices ease, MAIN higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West electricity prices ease, MAIN higher.

text.p: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity prices were mostly lower Wednesday with power in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) trading higher on some transmission restrictions, industry sources said.

Power from the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) was said to be restricted into the MAIN region. "We're drawing power mostly from the south," said one MAIN trader who added little spot and no hourly power was coming from MAPP.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for Thursday were quoted at $17.00-19.00 from a range of $18.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Tuesday.
Off-peak ECAR power for Thursday was said to be talked near $14.00 per MWh.
On-peak MAIN power for Thursday delivery was said to be in the $21.00-25.00 range with little power available from MAPP, from discussion at $16.00-18.00 on Tuesday, the brokers and marketers said.
MAPP on-peak power was pegged in the $14.50-17.00 range from $15.00-17.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Off-peak MAPP power was discussed near $8.50 per MWh.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for Thursday delivery was assessed in the $15.00-21.00 range from $16.00-22.50 on Tuesday, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
